text: {"answerable": true, "answer": "In a high-dimensional neural network potential, the total energy E is the sum of atomic contributions, E = sum_i E_i [W2025444507#003]. Each E_i comes from an atomic (sub)network whose input is a descriptor of atom i's local chemical environment, such as symmetry functions or an atomic environment vector [W2025444507#003][W2541404351#007][W4312043350#015]. All subnets share the same structure and weights for atoms of the same type, which keeps the total energy invariant when two atoms are interchanged [W2025444507#003]. The sum also lets the potential be applied to systems of different sizes [W2541404351#007][W2025444507#003]."}
